question.knowledge_point: Identifying When a Rational Function has no Vertical Asymptotes
question.worked_solution:
Let's simplify the expression by factoring both the numerator and the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4{x}^{2}-3x}{8x-6} & =\frac{x(4x-3)}{2(4x-3)}=\frac{x}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the denominator is never zero, we conclude that this function has no vertical asymptotes. A plot of the function is below. Note that it is not defined at $x=\frac{3}{4}.$
